legacy_root.title: Calibrate the duplicate threshold against a labelled pair set, reporting both error directions
legacy_root.question: At what threshold does duplicate detection minimise the DANGEROUS error - collapsing two records that each hold unique content - accepting more of the safe error, and what are the two error rates at the chosen point?
legacy_root.answer: Chosen lexical Jaccard threshold is 0.58 (version WFA-0098.lexical-jaccard.v1). At that point false_collapse_rate=0.0 (0 of 26) and false_split_rate=0.56 (14 of 25). Two-directional-divergence collapses=0. Balanced-accuracy would pick threshold 0.22 with false_collapse_rate=0.269231 and two_dir_false_collapses=6; a single accuracy number (0.823529 at t=0.22) is inadmissible because it hides the data-loss direction.

calibration.scope: LEXICAL token-set Jaccard. Embedding-scan artifact WFA-0008 and mutant-control artifact WFA-0096 are ABSENT on this worktree; this unit plants a labelled pair set covering the mutant classes those artifacts would have supplied (rename, paraphrase, fork, rewrite, known-distinct) plus two-directional-divergence.
calibration.estate_precedent: Measured on this estate: 100 percent of a comparable classifier's errors pointed at data loss. A threshold chosen on balanced accuracy therefore sits where the remaining errors are most harmful.

cost.rationale: false-collapse discards unique content from both records; false-split keeps a redundant copy. Estate errors were 100 percent in the data-loss direction, so false-collapse is weighted 100:1.

threshold_version.rule: Any change to this value re-runs every pair whose collapse decision flips, and refuses the change if two-directional-divergence pairs would newly collapse.
